utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, the document that you've just referred to, in essence, was a call to arms, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in late September of 1991, a Territorial Defence force was in fact raised as a brigade in the municipality of Prijedor, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prijedor TO unit mobilised and formed the Fifth Kozara Partisan Brigade, which was then deployed to western Slavonia in Croatia to fight along with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When that force first deployed after it was raised in late September of 1991, what was its ethnic composition?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The first deployment of this Fifth Kozara Partisan Brigade was -- corresponded closely to the national composition of Prijedor municipality as a whole, both by statements of the members of the National Defence Council and by the casualties that it suffered. It's plain that the force was probably a majority of Serbs but had substantial numbers of Muslims and Croats that were a part of it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Had the SDS prior to this time been critical of the JNA fighting in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: At the time the JNA withdrew from Slovenia in July 1991, the SDS board meeting reflected bitter criticism of the JNA for being insufficiently committed to the defence of Yugoslavia, and their closed-session comments were much more bitter than the public declaration, but both, in fact, reflected their disappointment that the JNA had not been more aggressive in Slovenia and had agreed to withdraw from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Were they less critical of the JNA's role in the war in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: They were less critical and openly prepared to support the JNA with volunteers, with actual deployment, of course, and with hospitality within the Prijedor municipality for units that either passed through or were stationed briefly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And indeed, the Fifth Kozara Partisan Brigade fought under the command of the JNA 5th Corps in Croatia, did it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's now time for a short break, and let's resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. I think they're just fetching Dr. Donia to the Court. Mr. President, one matter while the witness is coming. He is an expert who is testifying in another trial tomorrow and he will need to have contact with other prosecutors in the office, and I just want to ensure that there's no objection, either from you or the Defence, for that kind of contact. He is an expert, and certainly it's been normal practice in the Tribunal in the past that there is no kind of objection, but I just wanted to make sure that you are content with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You can be sure of that. What one Defence counsel and the Judges have in common is coming from a civil law system and we appreciate to have contacts between each other. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, I'd like to try and get through the balance of your evidence in the hour that we have remaining today, so I'm going to abbreviate certain matters. But I just want to remain with the 5th Kozara Brigade for a moment, and if I could refer you to Prosecutor's Exhibit 31, SK31, which is in your binder and is a public statement issued by the assembly of the Bosnian Krajina municipality, so the regional level of Serbian government that you previously referred to in your evidence. Now, am I right in saying that this is a document which expresses some concern about the safety of the Serbian population in Croatia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And because of that, the president of the assembly decides on a general mobilisation of Territorial Defence and public security reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And he also refers to a decision whereby the assembly had decided to end the shooting and killing of Serbs in Okucani and Stari Gradiska; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if you could briefly refer to appendix 6 of your report, and if that could be placed in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this is appendix 6, Mr. President, of Prosecutor's Exhibit 42. If it could be moved up, and if you could move it to your left. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, this decision, Prosecutor's Exhibit 31, refers to Okucani and Stari Gradiska. Can you point those out for us, please, Dr. Donia.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, I think it is not correct to characterise this document as a call for general mobilisation. It is indeed a statement that it will -- the ZOBK or the ARK may resort to a call to arms but is not specifically mobilising in a sense that that term is usually used in this context. The area to which this document refers is illustrated by the two lower arrows here on this map. It's from a somewhat later time. The map is from 1995. But for purposes of illustration, the Okucani town here and Stari Gradiska just north of the river in Croatia are the two geographic points of reference noted in the document we're examining.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And in the summer of 1991, to what region did the 5th Kozara Brigade of Prijedor deploy?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The 5th Kozara Partisan Brigade was deployed to this area of Lipik and Pakrac -- are the two towns that are mentioned in the reports of the unit's deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, can you describe the success or lack of it of the first deployment of the 5th Kozara Partisan Brigade to Croatia in the summer of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: That deployment saw substantial fighting. It was, I think, partially successful in supporting the JNA, but it led to a substantial desertion of over 200 troops in the unit. And when the unit returned to Prijedor in late October, the armoured column that brought the troops back, the soldiers who were on these vehicles fired long and loud into the air as they were entering Prijedor, and this was certainly regarded as an alarming display of firearms by the returning soldiers and was not welcomed by the Prijedor population.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I'm right in saying that on page 16 of your report you state that the Municipal Assembly voted unanimously, on the 7th of November of 1991, to remobilise the Fifth Kozara Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you state that the mobilisation order at that time represented an unusual compromise. Can you explain what that compromise was?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: All reservists were required to report at 8.00 a.m. on the morning of 8 November at the local military base. However, those who did not wish to join the military unit were asked to turn in their weapons and then were allowed freely to return home. Those who wished to join the unit were free to do so, and in fact were subsequently deployed back to the same area as the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of the 5th Kozara Brigade on this second mobilisation and deployment to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The second deployment was much more overwhelmingly Serbian in composition. It also suffered substantial casualties, all of which were named in the press reports at the time, and the vast majority of the names of casualties indicate that those warriors were Serbs, whereas the first person killed was a Muslim and was buried with great ceremony by the local Muslim religious leader in Prijedor, the vast majority of these were in fact Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When did the 5th Kozara Brigade return to Prijedor after this second deployment?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: In April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And how were they received when they returned to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: I don't know. There was a committee, a welcoming committee that was formed by the SDS to welcome them back, and what the exact nature of the reception was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you have your report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could go to the final sentence of the first complete paragraph, where you refer to the unit that returned to Prijedor in early 1992. My question perhaps was not specific enough, but that's what I was interested in.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just to read that sentence, "the unit that returned to Prijedor in early 1992 was made up of combat veterans who were lauded for defending Serbian national interests." I think my reference there was more to the ongoing praise that this unit received in the pages of Kozarski Vjesnik and other local organisations that were closely following, particularly Radio Prijedor, that were closely following the deployment in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And these combat veterans that returned to Prijedor in 1992 were predominantly soldiers of Serb ethnicity; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next part of your report, which deals with the plebiscite of the Serb people that was held in October of 1991. Now, if I can refer you -- I'm sorry. It's held in November of 1991. But if I can refer you to the minutes of the 28th of October, the minutes of the SDS municipal board.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, you will find these on page 421 of Exhibit SK12, which is the big copy, the large copy of the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Dr. Donia?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this particular set of minutes discusses the plebiscite to be held in November of 1991. Can you highlight for Their Honours the important parts of this set of minutes? Could you explain, actually, first of all, the nature of the plebiscite that was to take place in November of 1991.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. This document is titled, "Meeting of the SDS municipal board Prijedor, 28 October 1991." The sole item on the agenda is plebiscite of the Serbian people. On the date -- or at the first forming session of the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, those deputies of Serbian nationality who were members of the assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina and formed their own assembly in objection to the proclamation of autonomy or sovereignty by the Bosnian assembly. This body made its first order of business holding a plebiscite of the Serbian people to ask if they wished to remain in Yugoslavia. Non-Serbs were allowed to vote in this plebiscite, but they were given a different colour ballot and the formulation of the question was slightly different for them as well. It was thus the project of the SDS to secure the most possible votes in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia, particularly by the Serbian population, and in fact few non-Serbs anywhere voted in the plebiscite. At this meeting, we see the Prijedor SDS preparing for the plebiscite in Prijedor. The first sentence: "The chairman, Simo Miskovic, presented a report on the situation as the introduction to the meeting." He explains what the purpose of this is: "We are now at the stage when the state is being constituted, and all our efforts have to focus in that direction." One line down: "The results of the plebiscite, which will be held on 9 and 10 November, depend on our work."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, what state is Mr. Miskovic referring to there?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Well, this refers to a separate Serbian state which is in the process of being considered and set up by the SDS leaders of the Republic. Then his next-to-last statement: "Preparations for the plebiscite have to be carried out up to the last Serb, include refugees on electoral lists." The next paragraph assigns responsibility for particular areas. The last sentence there: "Stakic is put in charge of the former Omarska municipality." On the next page, 6 -- I'm sorry, 422, at the top of the page, ousted former party president Mr. Srdic says: "People living abroad should also be included, as well as those on the front lines. All refugees and the wounded in hospitals." Now, worth explaining that there were probably 5.000 or more refugees from Croatia in the Serbia -- or in the Prijedor municipality at this time, the vast majority of them were Serbs. The next paragraph is Mr. Vojislav Jokic: "We know how we fared at the elections and the census. This is our third chance." And halfway down the page, Milan Kovacevic: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "The SDS is in charge of the plebiscite, and the aim is the unification of the Serbian people." This document shows the effort of the SDS, the really organised endeavour to make sure that the most possible voters participate and vote favourably in the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, I'm right in saying that the plebiscite of the Serbian people actually took place on the 9th and 10th of November of 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What was the result of that plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, the vast majority of voters, 99-plus per cent, voted in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia, and very few non-Serbs participated in the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, what was the result of the plebiscite in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: I don't know the specific numbers. I don't have those numbers for Prijedor. The impact on the party, the SDS, was I think profound. It inspired the party to pursue the possibility of new elections because they became convinced, on the basis of the plebiscite results, that the majority of voters in Prijedor municipality were Serbs, and on this basis they sought to revise electoral lists and in a sense recast the November 1990 election in a new form so that they could this time gain a majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I can refer you to the minutes of the 22nd of November of 1991, which I think reflect what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you will find those, Your Honours, on page 427.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: This is entitled, "Minutes of the Prijedor SDS municipal board meeting, 22 November 1991," and at the bottom of this page, point 3, report on the plebiscite. In the Prijedor municipality area, the Serbian electorate makes up more than half the total electorate. The results can help us in future activities." The speaker here is Milan Pilipovic. And his last -- skipping one sentence: "The chairman proposed that new elections be conducted. It is necessary to adjust the voter registration lists by 28 November on the basis of the plebiscite lists. All refugees shall report to the public security station," that is, the police station," in order to be entitled to vote." And on page 429, the second speaker is again Milan Pilipovic, who says: "The main thing is to see whether we can gain power legally at the new elections." So the project of redoing the voter lists and proposing new elections for the Municipal Assembly gained great momentum in the results of the plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now refer to the minutes of the meeting held on the 2nd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Your Honours, you'll find that on page 431.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, this is a meeting again discussing the plebiscite, and I think Miskovic indicates, following the results of the plebiscite, that two options were available to the SDS in Prijedor. Can you please refer the Judges to the part of these minutes where Miskovic discusses those options?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. This is page 341, where Miskovic chaired the meeting, and then Miskovic delivered the introductory address. "The purpose of this meeting is to determine the best path to economic prosperity for Serbs in the municipality of Prijedor." Skipping one sentence: "The plebiscite vote has shown that 60 per cent of the electorate are Serbs. This indicates two options: 1, repeat the municipal elections; 2, take over and establish independent organs. It will be decided later which of the two options will be chosen."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, which option was in fact chosen?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The latter option was chosen not so much by a decision taken immediately by the Prijedor SDS as by an initiative from the SDS of Bosnia-Herzegovina's Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If on that particular note, if I could refer you to Prosecutor's Exhibit 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that, Your Honours, you will find behind tab 39 in your binder. This is a document entitled, "Instructions for the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in extraordinary circumstances." Mr. President, this is a document that, in a number of trials, has come in for considerable dispute between the parties, so we are going to spend some time discussing this document and try to establish its authenticity through other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What exactly is this document?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: This document is one of over a hundred numbered copies of a set of instructions from SDS headquarters in Sarajevo to those municipal SDS leaders in which any number -- any significant number of Serbs lived. So of the 109 municipalities in Bosnia, that would probably be 101 or 102 municipalities. The document makes some important distinctions between variants, and on the second page -- or the first page after the cover page of this document, in point 3, these are first spelled out. Variant A of this document refers to municipalities where the Serbian people form a majority, and Variant B consists of those municipalities where the Serbian people are not in the majority. So the document really is, in a sense, two separate documents, one for Variant A municipalities and one for Variant B municipalities. Turning to the next page, it makes a further distinction between a first stage, which amounts to instructions to prepare the institutional foundation for a takeover of power, and a second stage which consists of specific steps to be taken in actually taking power at the municipal level. Stage 1 and -- the first and second stage are each applied to Variant A and Variant B, so there's kind of a four-way -- or a division of this document. Now, on this page, which is 938, one sees that the first variant, variant A, has a total of six points on this page and an additional five on the following page, for eleven points in the first page. Going ahead to page 941, Variant B first stage, there are ten steps undertaken -- or recommended, instructed. And to try to make the distinction clear or the specificity of these steps clear, I've put them in an appendix, listing each of the ten points separately.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is appendix 7 of your report.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This, Your Honours, is appendix 7 of Prosecutor's Exhibit 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And I think, Dr. Donia, it will become clearer as we go through the SDS board minutes from Prijedor, the purpose of this tabular representation you produced; correct?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Because the language from this document from Prosecutor's Exhibit 39 is in fact repeated in those minutes, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Much of the language is repeated in the Prijedor SDS meetings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Indicating that they received these instructions at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it indicates that they received the instructions and paid very careful attention to the implementation of the steps recommended by the SDS Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I ask through you at this stage whether or not the Defence do in fact dispute the authenticity of Prosecutor's Exhibit 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We dispute the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. It should be clear for you now to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now refer, Dr. Donia, to an undated part of these minutes, which appears in the December 1991 section of the minutes.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. Page 435.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, you'll find this on page 435 of the SDS board minutes, and it is a set of minutes entitled, "Meeting of the representatives of the Prijedor municipality sector for military matters."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Donia, can you give an approximate date of this document, based on the minutes that appear before and after it?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The minutes immediately preceding this session in the volume are from 2 December 1991, and the subsequent meeting, next meeting, is on 27 December 1991. So this meeting logically fell between those two dates. And since it pertains directly to consideration of a document that is dated 19 December 1991, it is in all probability between the 19th of December and the 26th or 27th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the document of the 19th of December of 1991 that you're referring to are the instructions from the Main Board of the SDS that you've just been referring to, Prosecutor's Exhibit 39?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes, often referred to as the AB document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Judges the significant parts of this particular undated meeting.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: This is one of the few meetings which is not a meeting of the Prijedor SDS Main Board. It is entitled, "Meeting of the representatives of the Prijedor municipality sector for military matters." It is, however, presided over by Miskovic, the president of the Prijedor member of the SDS Main Board, who opened the meeting, reading now from the first paragraph, "who opened the meeting with a presentation of the instruction which had come from the assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, I note here that he attributes this to the assembly of the Serbian people, whereas the document that we just were looking at comes from the Main Board of the SDS party organisation. So there's somewhat of a discrepancy of his understanding of where it came from. He then enumerates ten points, and two-thirds of the way down the page, he gave the floor to Savanovic, who is in charge of these matters, he, Savanovic, briefly explained the forthcoming tasks. Now, what I have done is put the discussion as it exists here on this spreadsheet and left that in plain type. If we put this back on the ELMO, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So to make it clear, Dr. Donia, on it's left you have basically copied the exact language of Prosecutor's Exhibit 39, the SDS Main Board instruction of the 19th of December, 1991; and on the right-hand side you have taken the text from this undated meeting contained in the SDS board minutes, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 12, and you've put the language alongside each other to show that in essence the minutes represent language that is very similar or identical to that from the instructions issued by the Main Board of the SDS. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. The excerpts, quotes from this meeting we're looking at, are done in standard type, and the bold italic type is reserved for discussion at the next meeting in the Prijedor SDS minutes, 27th December.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. So on the right-hand side there are essentially text drawn from two meetings?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could briefly go through -- I think it's worth while going through that appendix.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Okay. I don't want to read the whole appendix, but just a couple of what I think are the key provisions in this document of 19 December 1991. The first point is "Introduce a system whereby all SDS municipal boards are continuously staffed and ensure uninterrupted contact and cooperation with all local communal boards in the municipality." This gets reflected in the undated meeting as: "Introduce round-the clock duty and uninterrupted communications, contacts with local boards on a daily basis are essential." And then it's again reflected in the meeting of 27 December 1991, with the language: "The problem of round the clock duty in the SDS offices and methods of maintaining constant communication with local boards. 1, introduce around the clock duty according to the roster we have agreed upon." Point 3 I think is important in the language of the SDS Main Board document: "The SDS municipal board will immediately form a Crisis Staff of the Serbian people in the municipality." This directive is reflected in the undated meeting as the municipal board will direct a Crisis Staff and the 27th December meeting with a somewhat more elaborate form, identifying in the same terms as the SDS Main Board meeting instructions, the members of that Crisis Staff. If we could go to just the next page, I will just take one more example, which is quite relevant, and that's number 4: "Convene and proclaim an assembly of the Serbian people in the municipality comprised of deputies from the ranks of Serbian people and presidents of SDS local communal boards." Now, this differs from the instructions for the formation of a Crisis Staff, which is just -- the local SDS is directed to form a Crisis Staff. In the case of the Assembly of Serbian People, it's also directed to proclaim it, and in fact, in all municipalities in which this took place, there was a public announcement of the formation of the Assembly of Serbian People in that municipality. In the undated meeting, that order is reflected with the language: "Convene a session and proclaim the assembly of the Serbian people," and in the 27 December 1991 meeting, results in a brief discussion about when this is to take place. The language is scheduling a date for the session of the assembly as the Serbian people of Prijedor, Stakic, 3 January, Gusuts [phoen], 6 January. Serdic does not agree because it's Christmas, which people celebrate at home. It eventually gets set for the 7th of January. But this same echoing of the language in typically more simplistic terms and often with an erroneous number to the corresponding document on the left-hand side goes through the remaining ten points of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, if I can refer you briefly to the minutes of the 27th of December of 1991, which you've already stated you've incorporated into this table that you've produced. Do you have those in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, could you please highlight in this document, other than what you've already said, anything of particular importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And these, Your Honours, you will find on page 438.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: This document is entitled, "Minutes of the meeting of the Prijedor municipal board of the SDS," held on 27 December, 1991. And in point 1, third paragraph, we note that Simo Miskovic again presides and makes an introductory presentation at this meeting, as he did at the previous one. At the bottom of page 439, assignments are given among party members to carry out specific committee formations. Second item on the agenda, designating persons to set up the committees. The first committee on inter-party cooperation is given to the president and vice-president, respectively, of SDS at that time, Simo Miskovic and Milomir Stakic. Other committee assignments are made and the committee for social affairs was also Dr. Stakic, and that was something on which he had at that time some previous experience working in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you go to the first page of that document, back to 438, and you see where there are numbered items from 1 to 5. And then underneath that, it states variant 2, capital letter "B" crossed out.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is that referring to?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Well, it appears to me that the notetaker here was uncertain whether this was to be the stage or the variant being discussed is probably not the first person to be somewhat overwhelmed by this document and its various designations. But clearly concludes that this is the -- B variant, or the second variant here, is the one which will apply to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the variant B version referred to in Prosecutor's Exhibit 39, the instructions from the SDS Main Board, is where the Serbs are not in a majority in a particular municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that was the case in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Let us now look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 45, which are, Mr. President, the additional documents that I referred to this morning that are not in the binders. And if they could be distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Mr. President, these documents are numbered 45 -- SK45, 46, 47, 48.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You don't. I have my copy, if ... This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 45. What is this decision?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: This is the decision on the proclamation of the assembly of the Serbian people of Prijedor municipality, reflecting a session held on 7 January 1992. This would therefore be an act indicating the implementation of .3, I believe, of the SDS Main Board instructions of 19 December. This was, as I indicated, a public meeting and produced a press coverage or a press report following this meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's actually, in terms of the instructions, from the Main Board, Prosecutor's Exhibit 39. It's item 4. But I just want to read the language, because I think it's important because it demonstrates a point you made a moment ago. Item 4 of variant B, the first stage, states: "Convene and proclaim an Assembly of Serbian People in the municipality comprised of deputies from the ranks of Serbian people in the Municipal Assembly and presidents of SDS local communal boards." So this decision directly reflects the instruction contained in Prosecutor's Exhibit 39, the instructions from the SDS Main Board, does it not?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Just to be clear on the perhaps terminology, Article 2 states the assembly has 69 members, including 28 representatives of the Serbian people from the Serbian -- that's the abbreviation for Municipal Assembly, okucani opstina. So those are the 28 SDS members of the Municipal Assembly, and then the presidents of the local boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, can I refer you to page 19 of your report. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, at the time of the time of the convening of the Serbian assembly in Prijedor, Dr. Stakic made a public statement, and you refer to that in your report. Can you explain to the Judges the nature of that public statement.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. Following the formation of the Serbian assembly, at which he was elected its first president, he was interviewed about the reasons for the formation of a Serbian assembly, because this was always very controversial and attracted considerable criticism from other parties. And he told the interviewer that the assembly was not directed against the Muslim people but against the irresponsible behaviour of leaders of the SDA in Prijedor, and he then stated, as he had earlier, that the SDA had avoided the agreement concerning division of authority - that would be the inter-party agreement - and seized all significant functions in municipal institutions, including National Defence, the municipal approximately court, the police, the prosecutor, and the public accounting service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is the accuracy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: The statement is not wholly accurate in describing -- it certainly is not accurate in describing the seizure, because most of these positions were taken by SDS nominees subsequent to negotiations with the SDS. That was the case with the National Defence Council, and of course the police, which we've already discussed. And it's true that the public accounting service and municipal court and prosecutor were at that time in the hands of SDS -- or SDA designees. It's partially inaccurate. It's partially wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Actually, I think you -- it was a slip of a tongue by you at one point. You stated that it certainly is not accurate in describing the seizure, because most of these positions were taken by SDS nominees, subsequent to negotiations with the SDS, and I think you meant SDA nominees.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: Yes. Pardon me. I meant SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move to -- actually, one question before that. Now, in terms of the SDS attitude to the Muslim leadership, this statement by Dr. Stakic, what did it represent in terms of the attitude of the SDS to Muslim SDA leadership in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: It was a statement that -- there was sort of a lack of confidence in the SDA leadership and at the same time a statement that the Muslim people were not the target of these SDS activities. But the approach to the SDA leaders was similar to what it had been on 17th and 18th of September, which was that they were acting in utter disregard of the agreements reached with the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Maybe for clarification, here the exact language of footnote 63 of your report, I have the impression it's not directly translated in the text. And additionally, do you have Kozarski Vjesnik of 10 January 1992 as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe we do, Mr. President. The two quotes that I gave at the bottom of page 19 are my translation and may not be what -- exactly what a professional translator would arrive at, but I did intend here to give you a full and accurate translation of the quote that is in the footnote. I'd be glad to read them, if you wish, for ... Okay. Let me just read the B/C/S of the first quote: "[Interpretation] Is not targeted against the Muslim population, but the target is the irresponsible behaviour of the leadership of the Party of Democratic Action in Prijedor." [In English] And then the second part, which is the indented quote: "[Interpretation] The SDA has persistently been avoiding decisions regarding the division of government and has taken all of the significant and important functions in the institutions of the municipality, such as the people's Defence, the municipal approximately court, the SUP, public prosecutor's office and even the SDK."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Dr. Donia, the president asked whether or not that newspaper article was incorporated into the bundle. I believe it is Prosecutor's Exhibit 40. If you could just check. I may be wrong. This is the article from Kozarski Vjesnik.

utterances.speaker: ROBERT DONIA
utterances.text: You're correct. This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 40, and the second page of that exhibit contains the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this additional clarification. Judge Fassi Fihri has another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have stated that the declaration is partly inaccurate. Does it mean that the reports also were partially inaccurate or just the declaration itself -- rather, the statement, not the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour's question to me was whether the statement of Dr. Stakic was in fact true and accurate, and it was my response that it was partially accurate but not completely so. The characterisation of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So are you referring to the statement or the facts contained therein? Is the statement itself accurate or not? It exists, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statement is, I believe, an accurate quote of what he stated, and his characterisation of these positions as being held by Muslims is accurate. I only take exception --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that the fact that Mr. Stakic is reporting about are partially accurate and partially inaccurate; would that be the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FASSI FIHRI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think I can go on if you wish. I think I'm going to go over into tomorrow for about 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would say if you can conclude five minutes to 2.00, we can do it today. So you would have another 15 minutes today.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'd like to take a bit more time over it than that. It may go over that. I'm not sure. I have a number of documents. It's not very long, but I think it might be better to finish with it tomorrow, if you're content with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. When you really can limit the estimated time to not more than 30 minutes, this would be the absolute deadline for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, Your Honour. It won't go beyond that. I'm just concerned that if we do go on, we won't finish and then Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. we'll have to leave because of the next hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right. Okay. Then the trial is adjourned and we meet tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
